papers.title: DS-Lighting: Making Agent Harnesses Explicit for Data-Science Automation
papers.innovation: Introduces and formalizes the concept of an 'agent harness' (task representation, state management, output constraints, evaluation feedback) for LLM agents, critical for improving end-to-end performance and governability in data science automation.
papers.benchmarks: Focuses on improving the practical and end-to-end performance of LLM agents by providing structured harnesses, addressing existing challenges in agent reliability.
papers.use_case: Building robust, reliable, and governable LLM agents for automating complex data-science workflows and broader AI agent development.

papers.title: The Signal in the Noise: An Auditable Reliability Layer for Biomedical Text Classification
papers.innovation: Proposes an 'auditable reliability layer' to systematically mitigate the impact of pervasive data quality issues (e.g., OCR artifacts, tokenization errors, character corruption) in large-scale text corpora on NLP pipeline performance.
papers.benchmarks: Addresses and aims to improve the degraded performance and reliability of NLP models, particularly text classification, when trained or evaluated on real-world, noisy data, with an emphasis on auditable results.
papers.use_case: Enhancing the robustness and trustworthiness of NLP systems in domains with inherently noisy text data, such as biomedical NLP, by providing a method for quality assurance and error mitigation.

papers.title: Statutory AI: Aligning Large Language Models With Legal Norms
papers.innovation: Develops novel approaches to align generative AI systems with evolving legal and ethical standards, addressing the shortcomings of existing alignment methods in achieving enforceable and interpretable compliance with regulatory frameworks.
papers.benchmarks: Focuses on establishing methods for achieving and demonstrating compliance with legal and ethical norms, rather than traditional performance metrics, thereby introducing a new dimension for evaluating AI system behavior.
papers.use_case: Ensuring that AI systems, especially generative models, operate in accordance with legal requirements and ethical guidelines, critical for deployment in regulated industries and public-facing applications.
